annotations.title: Section 179 vs bonus vs MACRS depreciation comparison

description: Compare the year-1 deduction and full depreciation schedule for an asset under Section 179, 100% bonus depreciation and regular MACRS. Use this tested BusCalc worksheet when the task matches its inputs and scope. Returns named results, units, formula, assumptions, method version, reference-value notes (official figure or your figure, with source and effective date), a check link and a source-page URL. Official reference values are prefilled when omitted; supply every other figure from the user's records. Percent fields take percent numbers. No figures are looked up; no private projects or purchases are accessed. Put tool fields inside inputs. Supply units or modelVersion only when listed in inputSchema. Follow its required fields and exact choices. Do not pass the REST calculator field inside MCP arguments.

bonusPct.description: Bonus depreciation rate (property acquired after Jan 19, 2025). Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. Official figure, prefilled from the source named below. Change it only if a newer or different figure applies to you. Official reference value 100% from IRS Notice 2026-11 (section 168(k) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21), effective 2025-01-20. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used.

convention.description: MACRS convention. Pick the option that matches your situation for the tax year. Options: half = Half-year (usual case); mq = Mid-quarter (over 40% of the year’s depreciable basis placed in service in the last 3 months).

cost.description: Asset cost (US dollars). Purchase price plus sales tax, delivery and installation.

income.description: Taxable income from the active conduct of your business (US dollars). Business income limit for Section 179, figured before the Section 179 deduction.

life.description: MACRS recovery class. Pick the option that matches your situation for the tax year. Options: 5 = 5-year property (computers, office machines, many light trucks and equipment — not passenger autos); 7 = 7-year (office furniture, most machinery and equipment).

limit179.description: Section 179 dollar limit (tax years beginning in 2026) (US dollars). Official figure, prefilled from the source named below. Change it only if a newer or different figure applies to you. Official reference value 2560000 USD from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32, section 4.24, effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used.

listed.description: Is this a passenger automobile or listed property?. Listed property includes passenger automobiles, other property used for transportation, and property used for entertainment, recreation or amusement. These have extra limits (section 280F caps and the more-than-50% business use test) that this calculator does not apply. See IRS Pub 946 chapter 5. Options: no = No; yes = Yes (passenger automobile or other listed property).

month.description: Month placed in service (tax year starting January) (month). Month the asset was ready and available for use. Sets the quarter for the mid-quarter convention.

other179.description: Section 179 already used on other property this year (US dollars). Reduces the dollar limit and income left for this asset.

otherProperty.description: Cost of other Section 179 property placed in service this year (US dollars). Used for the phaseout threshold test.

threshold179.description: Section 179 phaseout threshold (tax years beginning in 2026) (US dollars). Official figure, prefilled from the source named below. Change it only if a newer or different figure applies to you. Official reference value 4090000 USD from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32, section 4.24, effective 2026-01-01. Omit to use it; enter your own figure to override. The result notes say which was used.

use.description: Business-use percentage. Percent number: 6.2 means 6.2%. Share of use that is for the business in the first year.

modelVersion.description: Optional expected method version; a mismatch is rejected.

checkURL.description: Link that replays this calculation on https://buscalc.com/sumtru/verify/. Null when the inputs hold free-form text or the link would be too long.

notes.description: Reference-value notes first, then model notes and the standard limit statement.

referenceValues.description: One entry per official reference value in play: the official figure, the figure used, status official or user, source, effective date and the note text.

sealURL.description: Where a saved record of this result can be sealed with an independent timestamp.
